svg.title: Weight and balance terms: datum, arm, moment, CG
svg.desc: A board balances about the datum. A 50 pound weight at station 100 inches gives a moment of 5,000 inch-pounds (50 times 100). A 100 pound weight at 25 inches and a 50 pound weight at 50 inches on the other side give 2,500 plus 2,500, which is also 5,000 inch-pounds, so the board balances. Definitions: the datum is an imaginary vertical plane or line from which all arms are measured, set by the manufacturer. Arm is the horizontal distance in inches from the datum to the CG of an item, plus aft of the datum and minus forward. A station is a location named by its distance in inches from the datum, and the datum is station zero. Moment is weight times arm in inch-pounds. The center of gravity is the point about which the aircraft would balance, where the entire weight is assumed concentrated; it may be given in inches from the datum or percent of MAC.

Equal moments on both sides: the board balances
Any weight and distance whose product is 5,000 in-lb balances the board.
Datum and arm
Datum: an imaginary vertical plane or line from
which all arm measurements are taken; the
manufacturer establishes it
Arm: the horizontal distance in inches from the
datum to the CG of an item; plus (+) aft of the
datum, minus (-) forward
Station: a location named by its distance in
inches from the datum; the datum is station zero
Moment and center of gravity
Moment: weight x arm, in pound-inches (in-lb);
the tendency of a weight to rotate about a point
Center of gravity (CG): the point about which the
aircraft would balance if suspended there; the
theoretical point where the entire weight is
concentrated
CG may be given in inches from the datum or in
percent of MAC
